claim: Integrons are genetic elements that enhance bacterial evolvability through the acquisition of new genes encoded in integron cassettes.
source: Integrons are genetic elements that enhance bacterial evolvability through the acquisition of new genes encoded in integron cassettes (Francia et al., 1997; Escudero et al., 2015; Mazel, 2006; Hall and Stokes, 1993; Figure 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work (Francia et al., 1997; Escudero et al., 2015; Mazel, 2006; Hall and Stokes, 1993) and reference to Figure 1a.

claim: Integrons can stockpile arrays of usually promoter-less cassettes.
source: Integrons can stockpile arrays of usually promoter-less cassettes (Loot et al., 2017), and modulate their expression through shuffling events, providing a low-cost adaptive memory for the cell (Lacotte et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Loot et al., 2017 and Lacotte et al., 2017.

claim: Integrons modulate cassette expression through shuffling events, providing a low-cost adaptive memory for the cell.

evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lacotte et al., 2017.

claim: Some integrons were originally located on chromosomes.
source: Although originally located on chromosomes (Mazel et al., 1998; Rowe-Magnus et al., 2001), some integrons have been mobilized onto conjugative plasmids and have reached our hospitals (Escudero and Mazel, 2017; Rowe-Magnus et al., 2003; Ghaly et al., 2017) where they currently play a major role in the ecology of multidrug resistance among Gram negative pathogens (Gillings et al., 2008; González-Zorn and Escudero, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Mazel et al., 1998 and Rowe-Magnus et al., 2001.

claim: Some integrons have been mobilized onto conjugative plasmids and have reached hospitals.

claim: Integron integrases belong to the family of tyrosine (Y)-recombinases.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Mazel, 2006 and Nunes-Düby et al., 1998.

claim: Integron integrases form a discrete cluster within Y-recombinases that evolved recently.

claim: Y-recombinases typically recognize specific sequences on double stranded (ds-) DNA substrates and recombine them following an archetypical pathway of two sequential strand exchanges.

evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Grindley et al., 2006.

claim: Integrases have become a new paradigm in the field of recombination for structural and functional peculiarities that differentiate them from the rest of Y-recombinases.

claim: When cassettes are integrated, their sites (attC) are recombined as single stranded (ss) hairpins.
source: Indeed, when cassettes are integrated, their sites (attC) are recombined as single stranded (ss) hairpins (Bouvier et al., 2005; Francia et al., 1999; Johansson et al., 2004) while the site in the integron platform (attI) is canonically double stranded (ds) (Figure 1b).

claim: The site in the integron platform (attI) is canonically double stranded (ds).

claim: Structural constraints in integrases are solved through the acquisition of an extra α-helix (I2) within the catalytic core of the integrase protein.

claim: The I2 helix recognizes and docks a set of nucleotides that protrude from attC sites (the extra-helical bases).

claim: Two significant regions where mutations accumulated are: (i) the C-terminal domain where a high number of mutations mapped between the M and N helices, and (ii) the I2 domain.
source: We find two significant regions where mutations accumulated: (i) the C-terminal domain where a high number of mutations mapped between the M and N helices. Helix N serves as an anchor, burying one face in a hydrophobic pocket of the adjacent integrase monomer in the synaptic complex. It is necessary for the multimerization and stabilization of the tetrameric synapse. Mutations between helices M and N probably entail changes in the flexibility of helix N producing a different conformation of the synapse that better suits the processing of the more rigid attI sites. (ii) The I2 domain that is the basis for innovation toward attC site- processing (Nunes-Düby et al., 1998; Messier and Roy, 2001; MacDonald et al., 2006) only accumulated two of the 13 mutations suggesting it is not the major hindrance for the ancestral activity in modern integrases.

evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents an inference from the experimental results.

claim: The presence of Y220N (within the I2 domain) seems to correlate with higher double-strand exchange activity levels.
source: No single mutation is clearly responsible for these differences, but the presence of Y220N (within the I2 domain) seems to correlate with higher activity levels.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents an observation from the data.

claim: No mutations were selected in the first four α-helixes in the N-terminal part of the protein.
source: It is also of note that we did not select any mutation in the first four α-helixes in the N-terminal part of the protein, which form one side of the U-shaped clamp around the DNA target sites (MacDonald et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and supported by citation to MacDonald et al., 2006.

claim: The combinatorial library of 13 mutations has proven to be an efficient method to avoid the constraints caused by negative epistatic interactions and improve protein activity.
source: Our combinatorial library of 13 mutations has proven to be an efficient method to avoid the constraints caused by negative epistatic interactions and improve protein activity, as demonstrated by the 100-fold increase in activity obtained while keeping the total number of mutations equal.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents a conclusion from the experimental results.

claim: Epistasis was detected in a minority of cases (11/55) when studied systematically for pairs of mutations.
source: We studied epistasis systematically for pairs of mutations in our library, but could only detect it in a minority of cases (11/55, Figure 6e).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and supported by reference to Figure 6e.

claim: When epistasis was detected, it was more often negative (nine cases with significant negative epistasis versus two with positive epistasis).
source: When detected, epistasis was more often negative (nine cases with significant negative epistasis versus two with positive epistasis), suggesting that when there are interactions between pairs of mutations, the double mutant performs usually less well than expected.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents an observation from the epistasis analysis.

claim: The classical global epistasis pattern of diminishing returns associated to fitness improvement was not clearly recovered.
source: However, we did not clearly recover the classical global epistasis pattern of diminishing returns associated to fitness improvement (Kryazhimskiy et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and supported by citation to Kryazhimskiy et al., 2014.

claim: Models predict that epistasis between pairs of mutations is limited when the adaptive process is initiated far from the optimum.
source: However, models predict that epistasis between pairs of mutations is limited when the adaptive process is initiated far from the optimum, as it is the case here (Escudero et al., 2016; Blanquart et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Escudero et al., 2016 and Blanquart et al., 2014.

claim: When fitness gets closer to optimality, much more complex patterns of epistatic interactions are possible.
source: However, when fitness gets closer to optimality, much more complex patterns of epistatic interactions are possible (Blanquart et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Blanquart et al., 2014.

claim: The backward evolution approach used in this work contrasts with the ancestral sequence resurrection strategy.
source: In this work, we have shown that we could shed some light on integrase innovation using a backward evolution approach, in which a modern protein is evolved toward its ancestral function. This has to be contrasted with the ancestral sequence resurrection strategy in which a putative ancestral sequence is inferred phylogenetically, synthesized and evolved toward a new function.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents a methodological comparison.

claim: The process of ancestral sequence resurrection would be highly questionable for integrases because of long evolutionary time scales, the small number of IntI sequences available, and the lack of intermediates.
source: Here, the process of ancestral sequence resurrection would be highly questionable because of long evolutionary time scales, the small number of IntI sequences available, and the lack of intermediates.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents a justification for the methodological approach.

claim: The strategy used proved to be an efficient alternative that could be applied to other important switches in gene function that have occurred long ago.
source: The strategy we used proved to be an efficient alternative that could be applied to other important switches in gene function that have occurred long ago.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents a conclusion about the broader applicability of the approach.

claim: By strongly selecting for double-strand recombination, the authors managed to show that I2 is compatible with high rates of ancestral activity and that a route through functional intermediates exists between integrases in an early innovative state and modern integrases.
source: By strongly selecting for double-strand recombination, we have managed to show that I2 is compatible with high rates of ancestral activity and that a route through functional intermediates exists between integrases in an early innovative state and modern integrases.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents a key conclusion of the study.

claim: It is beyond the authors' reach to determine whether the route identified was the route naturally followed by integrases, or the impact that I2 had on the ancestor's activity.
source: Still, lacking an ancestor sequence inferred phylogenetically, it is beyond our reach to determine whether this was the route naturally followed by integrases (in opposite direction), or the impact that I2 had on the ancestor's activity.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents an acknowledgment of the limitations of the study.

claim: The authors cannot rule out that the rise of new functions in IntIs actually occurred through gene duplications.
source: Also, we cannot rule out that the rise of new functions in IntIs actually occurred through gene duplications.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents an acknowledgment of alternative evolutionary scenarios.

claim: Y-recombinases are abundant in phages, fomenting speculations about a viral (or partly viral) origin of integrons.
source: Y-recombinases are abundant in phages, fomenting speculations about a viral (or partly viral) origin of integrons (Escudero et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Escudero et al., 2016.

claim: The CTX phage of Vibrio cholerae is integrated as a ss-DNA hairpin, but it differs from integron recombination in that it is mechanistically identical to ds-recombination.
source: Interestingly, the CTX phage of Vibrio cholerae is integrated as a ss-DNA hairpin, but it differs from integron recombination in that it is mechanistically identical to ds-recombination.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents a comparison of recombination mechanisms.

claim: Xer proteins are the closest relatives to IntIs.
source: Xer proteins are the closest relatives to IntIs (Mazel, 2006), but do not contain an I2 domain to recognize ss- substrates and avoid the second strand exchange that would result in a lethal linearization of the chromosome.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Mazel, 2006.

claim: Xer proteins do not contain an I2 domain to recognize ss-substrates and avoid the second strand exchange that would result in a lethal linearization of the chromosome.
source: Xer proteins are the closest relatives to IntIs (Mazel, 2006), but do not contain an I2 domain to recognize ss- substrates and avoid the second strand exchange that would result in a lethal linearization of the chromosome.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents a comparison of protein features.

claim: It is possible that the acquisition of I2 occurred in an ancestor with Xer-like activity, and that it served initially to maintain the integrity of the chromosome when hijacked by ss-IMEXs that had not developed mechanisms to avoid the second strand exchange.
source: It is therefore possible that the acquisition of I2 occurred in an ancestor with Xer-like activity, and that it served initially to maintain the integrity of the chromosome when hijacked by ss-IMEXs that had not developed mechanisms to avoid the second strand exchange.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents a speculative evolutionary scenario.

claim: The results show that the ancestral integrase bearing I2 could have evolved without impairing the ancestral function up to a quite high activity on ss-DNA.
source: Our results show that the ancestral integrase bearing I2 could have evolved without impairing the ancestral function up to a quite high activity on ss-DNA.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents a conclusion from the experimental results.

claim: From detectable activity on ss-DNA, natural selection could easily drive the specialization toward the new function, even at the cost of impairing the ancestral function.
source: From that detectable activity, natural selection could easily drive the specialization toward the new function, even at the cost of impairing the ancestral function as our data show (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and supported by reference to Figure 7.

claim: The results suggest that the seemingly disruptive mutational event of acquiring an entire domain is compatible with a high ancestral activity, presumably thanks to the well-known robustness of the Y-recombinase fold.
source: Our results suggest that such a seemingly disruptive mutational event is compatible with a high ancestral activity, presumably thanks to the well-known robustness of the Y-recombinase fold (Kwon et al., 1997; Tóth-Petróczy and Tawfik, 2014).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and supported by citations to Kwon et al., 1997 and Tóth-Petróczy and Tawfik, 2014.

claim: An integrase with ancestral levels of ds-recombination activity and containing the I2 domain could have detectable levels of activity on ss-DNA upon which selection can act.
source: We further showed -see Figure 7- that an integrase with ancestral levels of ds-recombination activity and containing the I2 domain, could have detectable levels of activity on ss-DNA upon which selection can act.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and supported by reference to Figure 7.

claim: The data suggest that the peaks representing the ancestral and modern functions are connected by some form of ridge that may facilitate the transition from one to the other, fostering innovation.
source: Using the adaptive landscape metaphor -in which genotype space is plotted on the x and y axis and fitness on the z vertical axis- our data suggest that the peaks representing the ancestral and modern functions are connected by some form of ridge that may facilitate the transition from one to the other, fostering innovation.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents a metaphorical interpretation of the results.
